chunks.content: 96 That LOI Term That’s Screaming “I Have No Idea What I’m Doing” Hi Sara, If you've been firing off Letters of Intent (LOIs) like you're entering a sweepstakes—only to get ghosted, politely declined, or hit with the classic “we’ve decided to go another direction”... this one’s for you. Let’s talk about the one deal term that’s making smart sellers everywhere roll their eyes and move on: Zero. Percent. Interest. Seller. Notes. Yup, someone on YouTube (or maybe LinkedIn) made them sound like a genius move. But here’s the truth, straight from the trenches: it’s not savvy, it’s not strategic—it’s just a huge red flag. Why? Let me count the ways. Sellers aren’t ATMs. They’re not in the business of financing your acquisition for free. They want to get paid—and that includes interest on the money they’re essentially loaning you. Zero percent doesn’t incentivize payoff. If you’re the buyer, why would you pay early? There’s no financial benefit. You’d ride that note out to the bitter end. Not great for the seller. Here’s the kicker: The IRS hates it, too. They’ll treat that sweet 0% note as if it did have interest—thanks to a lovely concept called imputed interest income. That means the seller gets taxed as if they earned interest, even when they didn’t. Sounds fun, right? So when you throw a 0% seller note into your offer, you’re not just lowballing—you’re broadcasting that you don’t understand deal structure or tax implications. Not exactly confidence-inspiring. Bottom line: if you want sellers to take your LOI seriously, treat seller financing like the loan it is. Include a real interest rate, preferably one that aligns with the Applicable Federal Rate (AFR)—Google it. Want to stop making rookie mistakes that tank your offers before you even get to diligence? Check out Deal Academy, where I teach business buyers how to structure offers that actually get accepted (and don’t make sellers question your tax knowledge). To offers that don’t scream amateur hour, Sara Sharp Partner, SK&S Law Group Founder, Deal Academy P.S.
